description.plain:
DFRobot FireBeetle 2 ESP32-E is an advanced IoT microcontroller based on the ESP-WROOM-32E module, equipped with dual-core ECO V3 chips, offering improved stability, lower power consumption, and powerful wireless communication. As a versatile ESP32 development board, it supports WiFi + Bluetooth dual-mode, USB-C charging, and Arduino programming, making it ideal for smart home automation, wearables, DIY IoT systems, and wireless sensors.

With a compact stamp-hole design, the board fits perfectly into embedded applications while supporting rich I/O including UART, I2C, SPI, and more. Whether you're a developer or hobbyist using an ESP32-E module, it provides flexibility and performance with minimal power consumption for any Arduino ESP32 project.

Figure 1. Board Overview

Figure 2.Pinout

Espressif has recently released one wafer-level change on ESP32 Series of products (ECO V3). Below are the main design changes in ECO V3 Series of chips for your ESP32 WiFi Bluetooth applications:

1. PSRAM Cache Bug Fix: Fixed “When the CPU accesses the external SRAM in a certain sequence, read & write errors can occur”.

2. Fixed “When each CPU reads certain different address spaces simultaneously, a read error can occur.”

3. Optimized 32.768 KHz crystal oscillator stability, the issue was reported by the client that there is a low probability that under ECO V1 hardware, the 32.768 KHz crystal oscillator couldn’t start properly.

4. Fixed Fault injection issues regarding secure boot and flash encryption are fixed.

5. Improvement: Changed the minimum baud rate supported by the CAN module from 25 kHz to 12.5 kHz.

Key Features

  • ESP32-E dual-core microcontroller (ECO V3) with improved PSRAM stability and fault protection for IoT development

  • Supports WiFi (802.11 b/g/n/e/i/k/r) up to 150 Mbps & Bluetooth v4.2 connectivity

  • USB-C powered, onboard charging circuit & PH2.0 lithium battery interface for this IoT microcontroller

  • Ultra-low power consumption: average 2mA, deep sleep 10µA, ideal for battery-powered ESP32 development board projects

  • RGB LED, GDI Display Port, and onboard side key for user interaction with your ESP32-E

  • Pre-soldered header version for plug-and-play compatibility with Arduino ESP32 setups

  • Compatible with Arduino, MicroPython, and Scratch (future support)

Easy-to-Use ESP32 Development Board for Everyday Makers

The FireBeetle 2 ESP32-E is a compact and affordable IoT microcontroller designed for anyone looking to build smart devices and connected projects. The DFRobot FireBeetle 2 ESP32-S3-U is a compact IoT development board built on the ESP32-S3-U chip, featuring Wi-Fi, Bluetooth 5 LE, 8MB PSRAM, 16MB Flash, native USB OTG, and a U.FL connector for an external antenna. Designed in the FireBeetle 2 form factor with LiPo battery charging built in, it targets battery-powered Wi-Fi and BLE IoT applications where deep-sleep power efficiency, expanded memory for edge AI, and strong wireless connectivity are all required simultaneously.

Specifications

  • MCU: ESP32-S3-U (Xtensa LX7 dual-core @ 240MHz)
  • Wi-Fi: 802.11 b/g/n (Wi-Fi 4)
  • Bluetooth: Bluetooth 5.0 LE
  • RAM: 512KB SRAM + 8MB PSRAM
  • Flash: 16MB
  • GPIO: 26 usable GPIO pins
  • Interfaces: UART, SPI, I2C, I2S, USB OTG
  • USB: Native USB OTG (no CH340 chip required)
  • Power: 3.3V / 5V; LiPo battery charging via onboard charger
  • Dimensions: 25.4mm × 48mm (FireBeetle 2 form factor)

Key Features

  • ESP32-S3-U with U-shaped antenna footprint for external antenna support
  • 8MB PSRAM enables large buffer operations and TensorFlow Lite inference
  • Native USB OTG — acts as USB device without external USB-UART chip
  • FireBeetle 2 pinout is backward-compatible with FireBeetle ecosystem shields
  • Integrated LiPo charger for battery-powered IoT builds
  • Ultra-low deep sleep current for long battery life
  • Supports Arduino, MicroPython, ESP-IDF frameworks
  • AI acceleration unit for edge machine learning applications

Applications

  • Wi-Fi + Bluetooth IoT sensor nodes
  • Wearable devices with external antenna
  • Edge AI inference with TensorFlow Lite Micro
  • USB HID and serial device firmware
  • Smart home automation controllers
  • Battery-powered data loggers with deep sleep
  • BLE beacon and mesh networking nodes
  • MQTT IoT gateways

Package Includes

  • 1x DFRobot FireBeetle 2 ESP32-S3-U Development Board
  • Note: LiPo battery and antenna sold separately

FAQ

  • Q: What is the difference between ESP32-S3 and ESP32-S3-U? A: The -U variant has a U.FL connector for an external antenna, which improves Wi-Fi/BLE range significantly.
  • Q: Can I program it with Arduino IDE? A: Yes — install the ESP32 Arduino core (v2.x or later) and select the ESP32-S3 board.
  • Q: Does it support MicroPython? A: Yes — flash official MicroPython for ESP32-S3 and use Thonny or rshell.
  • Q: How long can it run on a LiPo battery? A: In deep sleep, current drops below 20μA. A 1000mAh LiPo can power it for months in light-duty sleep cycles.
  • Q: Is it compatible with FireBeetle shields? A: Yes — the FireBeetle 2 pinout is backward-compatible with DFRobot FireBeetle shields and expansions.

Bring edge AI processing and multimedia capabilities to local workbench setups with the DFRobot FireBeetle 2 ESP32-P4 AI Kit. Built around a dual-core RISC-V processor, this development platform handles hardware-accelerated video encoding and smart display management for custom Human-Machine Interface (HMI) panels or local AI cameras. It bridges the gap between basic microcontrollers and heavy single-board computers, making it an excellent choice for smart home automation builds.

Edge AI Processing with the ESP32-P4

At the heart of this kit is the ESP32-P4 dual-core RISC-V 32-bit processor running at 360 MHz, backed by 768KB of L2 cache. This provides the computational overhead needed for intensive edge AI processing without relying on cloud servers. Whether you are building a responsive HMI development rig or a local video streaming node, the integrated hardware H.264 encoding supports up to 1080p at 30fps, ensuring smooth multimedia performance.

Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5 Connectivity

Wireless communication is offloaded to a dedicated ESP32-C6 co-processor, freeing up the main RISC-V cores for your application logic. This co-processor adds robust Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5 LE capabilities, turning the board into a highly capable IoT gateway. It is ideal for smart home automation networks where reliable, high-speed data transfer is required alongside local video or AI processing.

Key Features

  • Dual-core RISC-V 32-bit processor running at 360 MHz for edge AI tasks
  • Integrated ESP32-C6 co-processor handling Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5 LE connectivity

  • Generous memory footprint with 32MB PSRAM and 16MB Flash

Gravity IO Shield for FireBeetle 2

Easy No-Solder Expansion for FireBeetle 2 Projects

The Gravity IO Shield for FireBeetle 2 makes it easy to connect sensors, displays, and modules to your FireBeetle 2 development board without soldering. Designed for the FireBeetle 2 ESP32-E and FireBeetle 2 M0, this compact expansion board brings the main IO pins out to convenient headers and DFRobot Gravity-style ports.

Vetco carries this FireBeetle 2 IO shield because it solves a common problem for hobbyists, students, and makers: connecting modules quickly without messy wiring or custom soldering. It helps turn a FireBeetle 2 board into a cleaner, easier-to-use project platform.

FireBeetle 2 Expansion Board for Sensors and Modules

This Gravity IO Shield is built to work with a wide range of DFRobot Gravity sensors and modules. It includes digital, analog, I2C, UART, SPI, and GDI connections, making it useful for sensor testing, small robots, environmental monitors, IoT devices, and display-based projects.

The shield gives you access to the FireBeetle 2 pins through female headers, making it easier to connect jumper wires, modules, and accessories while keeping your project neat and organized.

Why Buy This FireBeetle 2 IO Shield?

If you are building with a FireBeetle 2 board, this shield can save time and reduce wiring mistakes. Instead of tracking down pinouts for every connection or building a temporary breadboard layout, you can plug compatible Gravity modules directly into the shield and focus on the project itself.

It is especially useful for beginners who want an easier way to connect sensors, as well as experienced users who want faster prototyping and cleaner wiring on repeat projects.

No-Solder IO Shield with External Power Input

The Gravity IO Shield for FireBeetle 2 is designed for quick setup. No soldering is required, which makes it a good choice for classroom projects, hobby electronics, and quick testing at the workbench.

A PH2.0 power port supports 3.3V to 5.5V input, making the board useful for portable projects powered by an external supply or battery setup. The shield also includes an EN pin connection that can be used to cut power to the main board when needed.

GDI Display Interface for FireBeetle 2 ESP32-E Projects

This FireBeetle 2 IO Shield includes a DFRobot GDI display interface for connecting compatible DFRobot GDI display modules. This helps simplify display wiring by using a dedicated screen connector instead of requiring many separate jumper wires.

For display projects, the GDI interface is especially useful when working with the FireBeetle 2 ESP32-E and compatible DFRobot GDI screens.

Whether you are experimenting at home, building a classroom project, testing sensors, or putting together an IoT prototype, this FireBeetle 2 expansion board gives you a cleaner and more reliable way to connect your hardware.
